problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.statement:
Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return false if every element is distinct.

Input
The first line has n. The second line has the n integers of nums.

Output
Print true if any value appears at least twice, otherwise false.

Constraints
• 1 <= nums.length <= 10^5
• -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9

Example 1: nums = [1, 2, 3, 1]  →  true  (The value 1 appears at indices 0 and 3.)
Example 2: nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]  →  false  (All elements are distinct.)
Example 3: nums = [1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 4, 3, 2, 4, 2]  →  true  (Several values appear more than once.)

Difficulty: Very Easy · Topics: Array, HashSet · Target: O(n) time
Based on LeetCode #217: https://leetcode.com/problems/contains-duplicate/

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.statement:
Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.

Input
The first line has n. Each of the next n lines has one string (a line may be empty: the empty string).

Output
The starter code prints the answer in a fixed order, so any grouping order you return is accepted: the number of groups, then one group per line with its words sorted and separated by spaces (the empty string is shown as ""), lines sorted alphabetically.

Constraints
• 1 <= strs.length <= 10^4
• 0 <= strs[i].length <= 100
• strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

Example 1: strs = ["eat", "tea", "tan", "ate", "nat", "bat"]  →  [["bat"], ["nat", "tan"], ["ate", "eat", "tea"]]  (Words in each group contain the same letters.)
Example 2: strs = [""]  →  [[""]]  (The empty string forms one group.)
Example 3: strs = ["a"]  →  [["a"]]  (There is only one string.)

Difficulty: Medium · Topics: String, HashMap, Sorting · Target: O(n * k log k) time
Based on LeetCode #49: https://leetcode.com/problems/group-anagrams/

starter.python:
import sys
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def groupAnagrams(self, strs: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:
        # Write your code here
        return []


lines = sys.stdin.read().replace('\r', '').split('\n')
n = int(lines[0])
strs = (lines[1:1 + n] + [''] * n)[:n]
res = sorted(' '.join('""' if w == '' else w for w in sorted(g)) for g in Solution().groupAnagrams(strs))
print(len(res))
for line in res:
    print(line)

for line in res:
    print(line)

problems.statement:
Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

Input
One line with the string s (it may be empty and may contain spaces).

Output
The length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

Constraints
• 0 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4
• s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.

Example 1: s = "abcabcbb"  →  3  (The answer is "abc", with length 3.)
Example 2: s = "bbbbb"  →  1  (The answer is "b", with length 1.)
Example 3: s = "pwwkew"  →  3  (The answer is "wke", with length 3. Note that "pwke" is a subsequence, not a substring.)

Difficulty: Medium · Topics: String, HashSet, Sliding Window · Target: O(n) time
Based on LeetCode #3: https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-substring-without-repeating-characters/

import sys
s = sys.stdin.read().split('\n')[0].rstrip('\r')
last, start, best = {}, 0, 0
for i, c in enumerate(s):
    if c in last and last[c] >= start:
        start = last[c] + 1
    last[c] = i
    best = max(best, i - start + 1)
print(best)

problems.title: N-Queens
problems.statement:
The n-queens puzzle asks you to place n queens on an n x n chessboard so that no two queens attack each other. Given an integer n, return all distinct solutions. Each solution contains a board configuration where 'Q' represents a queen and '.' represents an empty square. You may return the solutions in any order.

Input
One integer n.

Output
The starter code prints the answer in a fixed order, so any order you return is accepted: the number of solutions, then every board as n lines of 'Q' and '.', boards sorted alphabetically (row by row).

Constraints
• 1 <= n <= 9

Example 1: n = 4  →  [[".Q..","...Q","Q...","..Q."],["..Q.","Q...","...Q",".Q.."]]  (There are two distinct valid arrangements for four queens.)
Example 2: n = 1  →  [["Q"]]  (A single queen on a 1 x 1 board is a valid solution.)

Difficulty: Hard · Topics: Array, String, Recursion, Backtracking, HashSet · Target: Exponential backtracking; commonly described as O(n!) search bound time
